checked_ok: The four FACT steps match section 6.3 verbatim (book p. 87): Step 1 identify DOFs, Step 2 the freedom space containing them, Step 3 'enough nonredundant constraints from the complementary constraint space', Step 4 '(Optional) redundant constraints ... for greater stiffness, load capacity, and symmetry'. The ball-joint case study is quoted correctly: the freedom space is 'the sphere of intersecting rotation lines shown as Type 3 in the 3 DOF column of Figure 6.1' (p. 87), its constraint space is the sphere of lines through the point (Fig. 6.8b), the three wires must 'not all lie on a common plane' (p. 87), and Step 4 is unnecessary except that the wires may be replaced by the kinematically equivalent stacked blades of Fig. 6.7a, as in Fig. 6.8d (p. 88). The 'fourth freedom the chapter warns of, p. 85' matches the p. 85 text about extra unwanted DOFs from too few independent constraint lines.

Screw algebra in fact/fact_core.py is right: recip = w.tau + v.f, and both constraint_space() and freedoms_of() are null spaces of the same Delta-swapped product, so 'reciprocal to every constraint' is computed correctly. The step-2 miss-distance test returns exactly the perpendicular distance (0.0500 for a 5 cm miss, 0.0010 for 1 mm) - a correct reciprocal product with a unit rotation, and correctly reported as outside the constraint space.

Step 3 reproduces: the 35 deg tripod leaves rank 3 / DOF 3, and I checked the three surviving twists have pitch exactly 0 and axis points exactly at C - a true ball joint, not a screw triple. Two wires leave rank 2 (4 DOF) and three concurrent coplanar wires leave rank 2 (dependent), as claimed.

Step 4's central claim is correct, and not merely numerically: a stacked pair of blades whose planes both contain the leg line has freedom space span{rot_d, rot_b(P1), rot_a(P2), trans_a, trans_b}, which I verified analytically is exactly the 5-space reciprocal to the wire's force line (rank of the union = 5). The 50-unit offset wire inside blade() does not fake the rank - singular values are 50/1/1 against exact zeros - and the three-leg joint then leaves rank 3 / DOF 3 as printed.

The leg-lengths-constant claim is exactly true in the model: flower_elastica.py:32-36 builds base_points and plat_points from the same head_axes(n) about the same P, so the hexapod is rigid in the head frame; over 200 random poses all six lengths are 1.446348433 m with a spread of 3e-15. The 1.45 m used for EA/L and the stroke is that length, the +-4 cm stroke is the u_fb clip at flower_elastica.py:236 and the 2 mm dither is at :219, and the runs' logged leg lengths (1.406-1.487 m) are exactly that envelope.

Sizing arithmetic that is independent of the two stress/rotation errors: P/(3 cos 35) = 1424 N and 5697 N per leg; strut EA/L = 200 GPa * 1.327e-3 m^2 / 1.4463 m = 183 MN/m for the 85 x 5.3 CHS of flower_elastica.py:97, which is wind_size.txt's own chosen section with its 16.1 Hz first mode; blade Euler 4 pi^2 E w t^3/12 L^2 = 80.4 kN and EA/L = 367 MN/m per blade; joint 3 cos^2(35) * k_ax/2 = 369 MN/m = 2.01x EA/L; two joints add 99 % compliance and drop the frequency 29 %. The K = 0.5 (no sway) end condition for the blade is defensible here because the orthogonal partner blade resists the block's sway in its own plane.

The 14 kN survival load per strut, though wrongly justified, is consistent with the audit's own 40 m/s wrench pushed through the flower's hexapod (8.6-12.5 kN per leg over head elevations 20-60 deg, J condition 2.1). Ti 6Al-4V at E 110 GPa and sigma_y 600 MPa is conservative (real yield ~880 MPa). Twelve joints x three legs x two blades = 72 blades, as stated.
The 'outside FACT' labelling is honest: the sizing block is explicitly separated from the four steps, and the register-page caption repeats that separation.

findings.problem: The coefficient 1.5 corresponds to no end condition. For a Euler-Bernoulli blade of length L whose ends carry a relative rotation theta and the relative transverse displacement that the ball rotation about C imposes, v = ax^2+bx^3 with v'(L)=theta, v(L)=delta gives kappa(0)=6delta/L^2-2theta/L, kappa(L)=4theta/L-6delta/L^2. With the blade's near end a distance s from C the kinematics force delta = s*theta, so the factor on E t theta/(2L) is 2*max(|3s/L-1|,|2-3s/L|): it is 1 only at the single placement s = L/2, and for a STACKED PAIR (the second blade necessarily has s2 >= s1+L) the best achievable maximum is 4 (blades at s=0 and s=L). The script's own drawn geometry (stacked_blades, line 41: blades at 15 mm and 45 mm from C, Lb 15 mm) gives 4 and 16. Correct stress for the chosen blade: 410 MPa (inner) and 1638 MPa (outer) at 1.6 deg, i.e. above the script's 300 MPa limit and, for the outer blade, above Ti-6Al-4V's yield. Re-running the script's own grid with factor 4 leaves ZERO feasible blades (I reran lines 64-71 with kfac=4: no (t,w,Lb) satisfies sigma<0.5 sigma_y, Pcr>3 P_leg_s and k_j>=2 EA/L simultaneously), so the chosen blade, the 154 MPa and the '369 MN/m = 2.0x the strut's EA/L' cannot all stand. The label is also self-contradictory in the handbook's own terms: Ch. 5 (Fig. 5.5, p. 59) defines a fixed-guided beam as one whose moving end is NOT allowed to rotate, and such a beam swept through a chord angle theta = delta/L has kappa_max = 6delta/L^2, i.e. a factor 6, not 1.5.
findings.fix: Replace the 1.5 with the placement-dependent factor 2*max(|3s/L-1|,|2-3s/L|) (>=4 for any stacked pair, 16 for the blade drawn at 45 mm), report sigma = 410 MPa for the current blade, and re-solve the sizing: the criteria as written have no solution in the grid, so either the blades must move close to C and grow in L (t 0.3 mm, w 90 mm, L 7 mm is the smallest feasible point in a wider grid at 1.6 deg), or the 2x-EA/L stiffness target must be relaxed.

(a) is a straight reading of the hardware. Line 74 names the element as "a constant-force element on a rolling diaphragm ... the gasometer's counterweighted bell is the gravitational original". A counterweighted bell (or a constant-force flexure stack on a rolling diaphragm) equilibrates the plenum against the constant force divided by the diaphragm area, referenced to whatever is on the diaphragm's other face — ambient at the bell. It therefore holds p_plenum - p_amb = const. The membrane's transmembrane load is Delta = p_plenum - p_face, and with a wind pressure p_w on the mirror face p_face = p_amb + p_w, so Delta = const - p_w: the wind passes through undiminished. The script's line 74 phrase "holds p_plenum - p_face at the pump's setpoint" and line 78's "the uniform part's 1.7-4.7 cm rms of defocus blur at 9-15 m/s goes to zero" both require the regulator to sense a pressure it has no port on. The finding stands but its fix is wrong in two places and misses the real correction.

The correct fix. Item 6 has the stiffness sign backwards. For gust rejection you want maximum plenum gas stiffness, not zero: the constant-force/gasometer element is precisely the wrong compliant element here, because it makes the plenum behave as if it were infinite. Replace it with a pneumatic low-pass — the smallest plenum the film's 1.93 m^3 stroke allows, deliberately sealed on gust timescales, connected to the pump through a restricted orifice of pneumatic resistance R. Above 1/(2*pi*R*C_eff) the orifice blocks and the trapped gas attenuates the face load by 1 + gamma*P*C/V_p (8-36x for V_p = 10-2 m^3); below it the pump sets the DC operating point and the RL policy trims the mean at its 20 s step. That is passive, sensorless, has no hysteresis, and needs no volume-swallowing bell, so lines 76-77 (the 1.0 m^2 diaphragm, the +-22 cm stroke, the 140 kg bell, the 0.15 m duct) go away entirely.

Then rewrite the affected outputs: (1) line 39 must state the plenum boundary condition explicitly rather than saying "(a sealed plenum)" while modelling an infinite one — give V_p and report 1/(1 + gamma*P*C/V_p); (2) the "none" rows' mean_left must be p_mean/(1 + gamma*P*C/V_p) if the case really is a sealed volume, which turns 3.3/6.0/9.3 cm into millimetres — or, if "none" is meant as "the blower runs at fixed command", say so and justify near-unity transmission from the fan's p-Q curve, since a constant-speed blower is a near-constant-pressure source at DC and the 3-9 cm may then be right for a different reason than the one written; (3) delete line 78's "goes to zero" and line 69's "or, better, the passive regulator of item 6"; with the low-pass the residual is the gust band below the orifice corner plus the item 4 gradient (2.13-5.91 mrad, unchanged), and the ranking in item 5 must be recomputed on that basis.
